   285→| **Output Messages** | Success and error message format | Usability requirement (REQ-002) |
   286→| **Integration** | End-to-end validation via CLI | System-level requirement |
   287→
   288→### Test Plan
   289→
   290→1. **Unit Tests** (`src/utils.test.ts` additions):
   291→   - `validateYamlSyntax()` with valid YAML
   292→   - `validateYamlSyntax()` with invalid indentation
   293→   - `validateYamlSyntax()` with unclosed quotes
   294→   - `validateYamlSyntax()` with malformed key-value
   295→   - `validateYamlSyntax()` with unbalanced braces/brackets
   296→
   297→2. **Integration Tests** (`src/yaml-validator.test.ts`):
   298→   - Valid file validation (exit code 0)
   299→   - Invalid file validation (exit code 1)
   300→   - File not found (exit code 1, error message)
   301→   - Output stream routing (stdout vs stderr)
   302→
   303→3. **Manual Testing** (pre-release):
   304→   - Real YAML configuration files
   305→   - Edge cases (large files, special characters)
   306→   - Performance validation (< 2 seconds for 1MB files)
   307→
   308→---
   309→
   310→## 8. Deployment Design
   311→
   312→### Entry Point Changes
   313→
   314→**Current** (`src/index.ts`):
   315→```typescript
   316→import { greet } from "./utils";
   317→const name = process.argv[2] ?? "World";
   318→console.log(greet(name));
   319→```
   320→
   321→**New** (`src/index.ts`):
   322→```typescript
   323→import { greet } from "./utils";
   324→import { validateYamlFile } from "./yaml-validator";
   325→
   326→const command = process.argv[2];
   327→const arg = process.argv[3];
   328→
   329→if (command === "validate") {
   330→  if (!arg) {
   331→    console.error("Usage: validate <filepath>");
   332→    process.exit(1);
   333→  }
   334→  await validateYamlFile(arg);
   335→} else {
   336→  const name = command ?? "World";
   337→  console.log(greet(name));
   338→}
   339→```
   340→
   341→### Backward Compatibility
   342→
   343→- Existing `bun run dev <name>` continues to work
   344→- New `bun run dev validate <file>` adds new functionality
   345→- No breaking changes to existing CLI behavior
   346→
   347→### Execution Path
   348→
   349→```bash
   350→# Existing usage (unchanged)
   351→$ bun run dev Alice
   352→Hello, Alice!
   353→
   354→# New usage
   355→$ bun run dev validate config.yaml
   356→YAML is valid: config.yaml
   357→
   358→$ bun run dev validate bad.yaml
   359→YAML error in bad.yaml at line 5: Unclosed quote
   360→```
   361→
   362→---
   363→
   364→## 9. Documentation Impact
   365→
   366→| Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale |
   367→|------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------|

   369→| add | src/yaml-validator.ts | JSDoc comments | patterns.md | Follow existing doc conventions |
   370→| add | src/utils.ts | JSDoc for validateYamlSyntax | patterns.md | Document new utility function |
   371→| edit | architecture.md (if exists) | Components section | architecture.md | Note new file handler component |
   372→
   373→---
   374→
   375→## 10. Design Decisions Log
   376→
   377→| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives |
   378→|----|----------|--------|-----------|--------------|
   379→| D1 | YAML parsing approach | Custom lightweight validator (no external deps) | REQ-004 forbids new dependencies; custom parser avoids adding `js-yaml` or `yaml` | Use existing npm package, shell out to external tool |
   380→| D2 | Validation scope | Basic syntax validation only | Matches in-scope requirements; schema validation out of scope | Full semantic validation, schema enforcement |
   381→| D3 | File I/O | Use `Bun.file()` API | Native Bun support, efficient async I/O | Node.js fs module, Deno API |
   382→| D4 | Command routing | Parse argv for "validate" subcommand | Simple, matches existing entry point pattern | Dedicated CLI framework (Commander, yargs) |
   383→| D5 | Output streams | stdout for success, stderr for errors | Unix convention; enables log filtering | All output to stdout, single output stream |
   384→| D6 | Exit codes | 0 for success, 1 for all failures | Standard Unix convention; simple for scripting | Different codes for different errors |
   385→| D7 | Error line number | Included in error output | User diagnostic requirement (REQ-002) | Generic error message only |
   386→| D8 | Single vs. batch | Single file per invocation | Scope constraint; simpler implementation | Validate multiple files in one run |
   387→
   388→---
   389→
   390→## 11. Technical Design Notes
   391→
   392→### YAML Validation Approach
   393→
   394→The custom YAML validator uses a **line-by-line tokenization strategy**:
   395→
   396→1. **Tokenize**: Split content into lines, parse each line for structure
   397→2. **Track State**: Maintain stack of indentation levels, quote states
   398→3. **Validate Rules**:
   399→   - Indentation consistency (spaces only)
   400→   - Quote pairing (single/double)
   401→   - Bracket matching
   402→   - Key-value colon placement
   403→   - Array marker validity
   404→
   405→4. **Early Exit**: Return first error encountered with line number
   406→
   407→**Why not a full YAML parser?**
   408→- Would require parsing complex YAML features (anchors, aliases, tags, multiline strings)
   409→- Would likely need an external library, violating REQ-004
   410→- Syntax validation is sufficient for catching common errors
   411→
   412→### Known Limitations
   413→
   414→- **Anchors & Aliases**: `&anchor` and `*alias` not fully validated
   415→- **Tags**: Custom YAML tags (e.g., `!!str`) validated minimally
   416→- **Multiline Strings**: Basic detection only; complex folding/block rules not fully enforced
   417→- **Escape Sequences**: Basic escaping checked; complex Unicode escapes not fully validated
   418→
   419→**Mitigation**: Document these limitations clearly. Users with complex YAML should use dedicated tools.
   420→
   421→---
   422→
   423→## 12. Hypothesis Validation (AFK Auto-Decisions)
   424→
   425→### HYP-001: Custom YAML Parser Can Validate Basic Syntax
   426→
   427→**Status**: PENDING
   428→**Risk Level**: MEDIUM
   429→**Statement**: A custom YAML syntax validator (without external libraries) can reliably detect common YAML syntax errors while remaining maintainable and performant.
   430→
   431→**Context**: The hard constraint of no new dependencies forces implementation of a custom validator rather than using established npm packages.
   432→
   433→**Validation Criteria**:
   434→- **CONFIRM if**: Implementation passes test suite covering common errors; startup time < 500ms
   435→- **REJECT if**: Parser misses obvious errors or startup time > 1 second
   436→
   437→**Suggested Method**: CODE_EXPERIMENT (prototype basic parser)
   438→
   439→### HYP-002: Bun.file() Error Codes Match Node.js fs Conventions
   440→
   441→**Status**: PENDING
   442→**Risk Level**: LOW
   443→**Statement**: Bun's file API returns error codes like ENOENT and EACCES for file I/O failures.
   444→
   445→**Context**: Error handling assumes Bun.file() throws errors with `.code` property.
   446→
   447→**Validation Criteria**:
   448→- **CONFIRM if**: Error handling code catches file not found and permission errors correctly
   449→- **REJECT if**: Error codes differ from Node.js convention
   450→
   451→**Suggested Method**: CODEBASE_ANALYSIS (test with actual file operations)
   452→
   453→---
   454→
   455→## Appendix: Command Usage Examples
   456→
   457→### Valid YAML
   458→```bash
   459→$ cat config.yaml
   460→name: my-app
   461→version: 1.0.0
   462→features:
   463→  - logging
   464→  - monitoring
   465→
   466→$ bun run dev validate config.yaml
   467→YAML is valid: config.yaml
   468→$ echo $?
   469→0
   470→```
   471→
   472→### Invalid YAML (unclosed quote)
   473→```bash
   474→$ cat bad.yaml
   475→name: "my-app
   476→version: 1.0.0
   477→
   478→$ bun run dev validate bad.yaml
   479→YAML error in bad.yaml at line 1: Unclosed quote
   480→$ echo $?
   481→1
   482→```
   483→
   484→### File not found
   485→```bash
   486→$ bun run dev validate nonexistent.yaml
   487→File not found: nonexistent.yaml
   488→$ echo $?
   489→1
   490→```
   491→

    13→## 1. Design Overview
    14→
    15→This feature adds a command-line YAML validator to the rp1-eval-project. The validator:
    16→- Accepts a file path as input

    24→
    25→```
    26→User Command (CLI)
    27→    ↓
    28→src/index.ts (command router)
    29→    ↓
    30→src/yaml-validator.ts (handler)

    45→|-----------|---------|----------|
    46→| YAML Syntax Validator | Core validation logic | `src/utils.ts` (new export) |
    47→| File Handler | Reads file, manages I/O errors | `src/yaml-validator.ts` (new) |
    48→| Command Router | Routes CLI commands to handlers | `src/index.ts` (modified) |
    49→| Tests | Validation & integration tests | `src/yaml-validator.test.ts` (new) |
    50→

    52→
    53→```
    54→1. User runs: bun run dev validate <filepath>
    55→2. index.ts parses argv, detects "validate" command
    56→3. yaml-validator.ts:
    57→   a. Reads file content via Bun.file()
    58→   b. Calls validateYamlSyntax(content)
    59→   c. Formats and outputs result
    60→4. Process exits with appropriate code (0 or 1+)
    61→```
    62→
    63→### Validation Result Contract
    64→
    65→```typescript
    66→interface YamlValidationResult {
    67→  valid: boolean;
    68→  error?: {
    69→    line: number;
    70→    column?: number;
    71→    message: string;
    72→  };
    73→}
    74→```
    75→
    76→---
    77→
    78→## 3. Detailed Design
    79→
    80→### 3.1 YAML Syntax Validator (`src/utils.ts` - New Export)
    81→
    82→**Function**: `validateYamlSyntax(content: string): YamlValidationResult`
    83→
    84→**Validation Rules** (Scope: Basic YAML 1.2 Syntax):
    85→
    86→1. **Indentation**:
    87→   - Consistent indentation (spaces only, no tabs)
    88→   - Valid nesting levels
    89→
    90→2. **Structure Markers**:
    91→   - Paired quotes (single and double)
    92→   - Balanced brackets and braces
    93→   - Valid array markers (-)
    94→   - Valid key-value pairs (:)
    95→
    96→3. **Comments**:
    97→   - Hash (#) comments allowed anywhere
    98→
    99→4. **Strings**:
   100→   - Quoted strings with proper escaping
   101→   - Unquoted strings (basic validation)
   102→   - Multiline strings (basic block detection)
   103→
   104→5. **Collections**:
   105→   - Maps (key: value syntax)
   106→   - Sequences (- item syntax)
   107→   - Nested structures
   108→
   109→**Algorithm**: Line-by-line tokenization with state tracking:
   110→- Track indentation stack
   111→- Detect unclosed quotes
   112→- Validate key-value colons
   113→- Check array marker placement
   114→
   115→**Error Reporting**:
   116→- Return line number and column (if detectable)
   117→- Descriptive message (e.g., "Unclosed quote on line 5")
   118→
   119→**Limitations** (Documented):
   120→- Does not validate against YAML schema
   121→- Does not parse anchors/aliases in detail
   122→- Does not resolve YAML tags
   123→- Focuses on syntactic structure only
   124→
   125→### 3.2 File Handler (`src/yaml-validator.ts` - New File)
   126→
   127→**Function**: `validateYamlFile(filePath: string): Promise<void>`
   128→
   129→**Responsibilities**:
   130→1. Read file using `Bun.file()`
   131→2. Call `validateYamlSyntax()`
   132→3. Format and output results
   133→4. Handle errors (file not found, permission denied, read errors)
   134→5. Exit with appropriate code
   135→
   136→**Error Handling**:
   137→```typescript
   138→try {
   139→  const content = await Bun.file(filePath).text();
   140→  const result = validateYamlSyntax(content);
   141→
   142→  if (result.valid) {
   143→    console.log(`YAML is valid: ${filePath}`);
   144→    process.exit(0);
   145→  } else {
   146→    console.error(
   147→      `YAML error in ${filePath} at line ${result.error.line}: ${result.error.message}`
   148→    );
   149→    process.exit(1);
   150→  }
   151→} catch (error) {
   152→  if (error.code === 'ENOENT') {
   153→    console.error(`File not found: ${filePath}`);
   154→  } else if (error.code === 'EACCES') {
   155→    console.error(`Permission denied: ${filePath}`);
   156→  } else {
   157→    console.error(`Error reading file: ${error.message}`);
   158→  }
   159→  process.exit(1);
   160→}
   161→```
   162→
   163→**Output Streams**:
   164→- **stdout**: Success messages and validation confirmations
   165→- **stderr**: Error messages and diagnostics

   171→| Layer | Technology | Rationale |

   173→| Runtime | Bun 1.3.12+ | Already in use; provides fast execution |
   174→| Language | TypeScript (strict mode) | Existing project standard |
   175→| YAML Parsing | Custom syntax validator | No external dependencies allowed; implements basic validation |
   176→| File I/O | `Bun.file()` API | Native Bun support; efficient async file reading |
   177→| Testing | Bun's built-in test runner | Consistent with existing test pattern |
   178→| CLI | `process.argv` | Lightweight; existing pattern in index.ts |

   310→## 8. Deployment Design
   311→
   312→### Entry Point Changes
   313→
   314→**Current** (`src/index.ts`):

   320→
   321→**New** (`src/index.ts`):
   322→```typescript
   323→import { greet } from "./utils";
   324→import { validateYamlFile } from "./yaml-validator";
   325→
   326→const command = process.argv[2];
   327→const arg = process.argv[3];
   328→
   329→if (command === "validate") {
   330→  if (!arg) {
   331→    console.error("Usage: validate <filepath>");
   332→    process.exit(1);
   333→  }
   334→  await validateYamlFile(arg);
   335→} else {
   336→  const name = command ?? "World";

   338→}

   344→- New `bun run dev validate <file>` adds new functionality

   346→
   347→### Execution Path
   348→
   349→```bash
   350→# Existing usage (unchanged)
   351→$ bun run dev Alice
   352→Hello, Alice!
   353→
   354→# New usage
   355→$ bun run dev validate config.yaml

   357→
   358→$ bun run dev validate bad.yaml

   360→```

   365→

   374→
   375→## 10. Design Decisions Log
   376→
   377→| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives |
   378→|----|----------|--------|-----------|--------------|
   379→| D1 | YAML parsing approach | Custom lightweight validator (no external deps) | REQ-004 forbids new dependencies; custom parser avoids adding `js-yaml` or `yaml` | Use existing npm package, shell out to external tool |
   380→| D2 | Validation scope | Basic syntax validation only | Matches in-scope requirements; schema validation out of scope | Full semantic validation, schema enforcement |
   381→| D3 | File I/O | Use `Bun.file()` API | Native Bun support, efficient async I/O | Node.js fs module, Deno API |
   382→| D4 | Command routing | Parse argv for "validate" subcommand | Simple, matches existing entry point pattern | Dedicated CLI framework (Commander, yargs) |
   383→| D5 | Output streams | stdout for success, stderr for errors | Unix convention; enables log filtering | All output to stdout, single output stream |
   384→| D6 | Exit codes | 0 for success, 1 for all failures | Standard Unix convention; simple for scripting | Different codes for different errors |
   385→| D7 | Error line number | Included in error output | User diagnostic requirement (REQ-002) | Generic error message only |
   386→| D8 | Single vs. batch | Single file per invocation | Scope constraint; simpler implementation | Validate multiple files in one run |
   387→
   388→---
   389→
   390→## 11. Technical Design Notes
   391→
   392→### YAML Validation Approach
   393→
   394→The custom YAML validator uses a **line-by-line tokenization strategy**:
   395→
   396→1. **Tokenize**: Split content into lines, parse each line for structure
   397→2. **Track State**: Maintain stack of indentation levels, quote states
   398→3. **Validate Rules**:
   399→   - Indentation consistency (spaces only)
   400→   - Quote pairing (single/double)
   401→   - Bracket matching
   402→   - Key-value colon placement
   403→   - Array marker validity
   404→
   405→4. **Early Exit**: Return first error encountered with line number
   406→
   407→**Why not a full YAML parser?**
   408→- Would require parsing complex YAML features (anchors, aliases, tags, multiline strings)
   409→- Would likely need an external library, violating REQ-004
   410→- Syntax validation is sufficient for catching common errors
   411→
   412→### Known Limitations
   413→
   414→- **Anchors & Aliases**: `&anchor` and `*alias` not fully validated
   415→- **Tags**: Custom YAML tags (e.g., `!!str`) validated minimally
   416→- **Multiline Strings**: Basic detection only; complex folding/block rules not fully enforced
   417→- **Escape Sequences**: Basic escaping checked; complex Unicode escapes not fully validated
   418→
   419→**Mitigation**: Document these limitations clearly. Users with complex YAML should use dedicated tools.
   420→
   421→---
   422→
   423→## 12. Hypothesis Validation (AFK Auto-Decisions)
   424→
   425→### HYP-001: Custom YAML Parser Can Validate Basic Syntax
   426→
   427→**Status**: PENDING

   430→
   431→**Context**: The hard constraint of no new dependencies forces implementation of a custom validator rather than using established npm packages.
   432→
   433→**Validation Criteria**:
   434→- **CONFIRM if**: Implementation passes test suite covering common errors; startup time < 500ms
   435→- **REJECT if**: Parser misses obvious errors or startup time > 1 second
   436→
   437→**Suggested Method**: CODE_EXPERIMENT (prototype basic parser)
   438→
   439→### HYP-002: Bun.file() Error Codes Match Node.js fs Conventions
   440→
   441→**Status**: PENDING
   442→**Risk Level**: LOW
   443→**Statement**: Bun's file API returns error codes like ENOENT and EACCES for file I/O failures.
   444→
   445→**Context**: Error handling assumes Bun.file() throws errors with `.code` property.
   446→
   447→**Validation Criteria**:
   448→- **CONFIRM if**: Error handling code catches file not found and permission errors correctly
   449→- **REJECT if**: Error codes differ from Node.js convention
   450→
   451→**Suggested Method**: CODEBASE_ANALYSIS (test with actual file operations)
   452→
   453→---
   454→
   455→## Appendix: Command Usage Examples
   456→
   457→### Valid YAML
   458→```bash
   459→$ cat config.yaml
   460→name: my-app
   461→version: 1.0.0
   462→features:
   463→  - logging
   464→  - monitoring
   465→
   466→$ bun run dev validate config.yaml
   467→YAML is valid: config.yaml
   468→$ echo $?
   469→0
   470→```
   471→
   472→### Invalid YAML (unclosed quote)
   473→```bash
   474→$ cat bad.yaml
   475→name: "my-app
   476→version: 1.0.0
   477→
   478→$ bun run dev validate bad.yaml
   479→YAML error in bad.yaml at line 1: Unclosed quote
   480→$ echo $?
   481→1
   482→```
   483→
   484→### File not found
   485→```bash
   486→$ bun run dev validate nonexistent.yaml
   487→File not found: nonexistent.yaml
   488→$ echo $?
   489→1
   490→```

     5→
     6→# Design Document: Simple YAML Validator Command
     7→
     8→**Feature ID**: add a simple yaml validator command without adding new deps
     9→**Version**: 1.0.0
    10→**Created**: 2026-04-11
    11→**Status**: Design Phase
    12→
    13→## 1. Design Overview
    14→
    15→This feature adds a command-line YAML validator to the rp1-eval-project. The validator:
    16→- Accepts a file path as input
    17→- Validates YAML syntax without external dependencies
    18→- Returns appropriate exit codes and user-friendly error messages
    19→- Integrates seamlessly with the existing Bun/TypeScript entry point pattern
    20→
    21→**Key Constraint**: Implementation uses only existing dependencies (TypeScript, Bun, stdlib). A lightweight custom YAML syntax validator replaces external packages.
    22→
    23→### High-Level Architecture
    24→
    25→```
    26→User Command (CLI)
    27→    ↓
    28→src/index.ts (command router)
    29→    ↓
    30→src/yaml-validator.ts (handler)
    31→    ├─ File I/O (Bun.file)
    32→    ├─ validateYamlSyntax() (from utils)
    33→    └─ Output formatting
    34→    ↓
    35→Exit code + stdout/stderr output
    36→```
    37→
    38→---
    39→
    40→## 2. Architecture
    41→
    42→### Component Overview
    43→
    44→| Component | Purpose | Location |
    45→|-----------|---------|----------|
    46→| YAML Syntax Validator | Core validation logic | `src/utils.ts` (new export) |
    47→| File Handler | Reads file, manages I/O errors | `src/yaml-validator.ts` (new) |
    48→| Command Router | Routes CLI commands to handlers | `src/index.ts` (modified) |
    49→| Tests | Validation & integration tests | `src/yaml-validator.test.ts` (new) |
    50→
    51→### Data Flow
    52→
    53→```
    54→1. User runs: bun run dev validate <filepath>
    55→2. index.ts parses argv, detects "validate" command
    56→3. yaml-validator.ts:
    57→   a. Reads file content via Bun.file()
    58→   b. Calls validateYamlSyntax(content)
    59→   c. Formats and outputs result
    60→4. Process exits with appropriate code (0 or 1+)
    61→```
    62→
    63→### Validation Result Contract
    64→
    65→```typescript
    66→interface YamlValidationResult {
    67→  valid: boolean;
    68→  error?: {
    69→    line: number;
    70→    column?: number;
    71→    message: string;
    72→  };
    73→}
    74→```
    75→
    76→---
    77→
    78→## 3. Detailed Design
    79→
    80→### 3.1 YAML Syntax Validator (`src/utils.ts` - New Export)
    81→
    82→**Function**: `validateYamlSyntax(content: string): YamlValidationResult`
    83→
    84→**Validation Rules** (Scope: Basic YAML 1.2 Syntax):
    85→
    86→1. **Indentation**:
    87→   - Consistent indentation (spaces only, no tabs)
    88→   - Valid nesting levels
    89→
    90→2. **Structure Markers**:
    91→   - Paired quotes (single and double)
    92→   - Balanced brackets and braces
    93→   - Valid array markers (-)
    94→   - Valid key-value pairs (:)
    95→
    96→3. **Comments**:
    97→   - Hash (#) comments allowed anywhere
    98→
    99→4. **Strings**:
   100→   - Quoted strings with proper escaping
   101→   - Unquoted strings (basic validation)
   102→   - Multiline strings (basic block detection)
   103→
   104→5. **Collections**:
   105→   - Maps (key: value syntax)
   106→   - Sequences (- item syntax)
   107→   - Nested structures
   108→
   109→**Algorithm**: Line-by-line tokenization with state tracking:
   110→- Track indentation stack
   111→- Detect unclosed quotes
   112→- Validate key-value colons
   113→- Check array marker placement
   114→
   115→**Error Reporting**:
   116→- Return line number and column (if detectable)
   117→- Descriptive message (e.g., "Unclosed quote on line 5")
   118→
   119→**Limitations** (Documented):
   120→- Does not validate against YAML schema
   121→- Does not parse anchors/aliases in detail
   122→- Does not resolve YAML tags
   123→- Focuses on syntactic structure only
   124→
   125→### 3.2 File Handler (`src/yaml-validator.ts` - New File)
   126→
   127→**Function**: `validateYamlFile(filePath: string): Promise<void>`
   128→
   129→**Responsibilities**:
   130→1. Read file using `Bun.file()`
   131→2. Call `validateYamlSyntax()`
   132→3. Format and output results
   133→4. Handle errors (file not found, permission denied, read errors)
   134→5. Exit with appropriate code
   135→
   136→**Error Handling**:
   137→```typescript
   138→try {
   139→  const content = await Bun.file(filePath).text();
   140→  const result = validateYamlSyntax(content);
   141→
   142→  if (result.valid) {
   143→    console.log(`YAML is valid: ${filePath}`);
   144→    process.exit(0);
   145→  } else {
   146→    console.error(
   147→      `YAML error in ${filePath} at line ${result.error.line}: ${result.error.message}`
   148→    );
   149→    process.exit(1);
   150→  }
   151→} catch (error) {

   310→## 8. Deployment Design
   311→
   312→### Entry Point Changes
   313→
   314→**Current** (`src/index.ts`):

   320→
   321→**New** (`src/index.ts`):
   322→```typescript
   323→import { greet } from "./utils";
   324→import { validateYamlFile } from "./yaml-validator";
   325→
   326→const command = process.argv[2];
   327→const arg = process.argv[3];
   328→
   329→if (command === "validate") {
   330→  if (!arg) {
   331→    console.error("Usage: validate <filepath>");
   332→    process.exit(1);
   333→  }
   334→  await validateYamlFile(arg);
   335→} else {
   336→  const name = command ?? "World";
   337→  console.log(greet(name));
   338→}

   346→
   347→### Execution Path
   348→
   349→```bash
   350→# Existing usage (unchanged)
   351→$ bun run dev Alice
   352→Hello, Alice!
   353→
   354→# New usage
   355→$ bun run dev validate config.yaml

   357→

   360→```

   365→

   372→
   373→---
   374→
   375→## 10. Design Decisions Log
   376→
   377→| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives |
   378→|----|----------|--------|-----------|--------------|
   379→| D1 | YAML parsing approach | Custom lightweight validator (no external deps) | REQ-004 forbids new dependencies; custom parser avoids adding `js-yaml` or `yaml` | Use existing npm package, shell out to external tool |
   380→| D2 | Validation scope | Basic syntax validation only | Matches in-scope requirements; schema validation out of scope | Full semantic validation, schema enforcement |
   381→| D3 | File I/O | Use `Bun.file()` API | Native Bun support, efficient async I/O | Node.js fs module, Deno API |
   382→| D4 | Command routing | Parse argv for "validate" subcommand | Simple, matches existing entry point pattern | Dedicated CLI framework (Commander, yargs) |
   383→| D5 | Output streams | stdout for success, stderr for errors | Unix convention; enables log filtering | All output to stdout, single output stream |
   384→| D6 | Exit codes | 0 for success, 1 for all failures | Standard Unix convention; simple for scripting | Different codes for different errors |
   385→| D7 | Error line number | Included in error output | User diagnostic requirement (REQ-002) | Generic error message only |
   386→| D8 | Single vs. batch | Single file per invocation | Scope constraint; simpler implementation | Validate multiple files in one run |
   387→
   388→---
   389→
   390→## 11. Technical Design Notes
   391→
   392→### YAML Validation Approach
   393→
   394→The custom YAML validator uses a **line-by-line tokenization strategy**:
   395→
   396→1. **Tokenize**: Split content into lines, parse each line for structure
   397→2. **Track State**: Maintain stack of indentation levels, quote states
   398→3. **Validate Rules**:
   399→   - Indentation consistency (spaces only)
   400→   - Quote pairing (single/double)
   401→   - Bracket matching
   402→   - Key-value colon placement
   403→   - Array marker validity
   404→
   405→4. **Early Exit**: Return first error encountered with line number
   406→
   407→**Why not a full YAML parser?**
   408→- Would require parsing complex YAML features (anchors, aliases, tags, multiline strings)
   409→- Would likely need an external library, violating REQ-004
   410→- Syntax validation is sufficient for catching common errors
   411→
   412→### Known Limitations
   413→
   414→- **Anchors & Aliases**: `&anchor` and `*alias` not fully validated
   415→- **Tags**: Custom YAML tags (e.g., `!!str`) validated minimally
   416→- **Multiline Strings**: Basic detection only; complex folding/block rules not fully enforced
   417→- **Escape Sequences**: Basic escaping checked; complex Unicode escapes not fully validated
   418→
   419→**Mitigation**: Document these limitations clearly. Users with complex YAML should use dedicated tools.
   420→
   421→---
   422→
   423→## 12. Hypothesis Validation (AFK Auto-Decisions)
   424→
   425→### HYP-001: Custom YAML Parser Can Validate Basic Syntax
   426→
   427→**Status**: PENDING
   428→**Risk Level**: MEDIUM
   429→**Statement**: A custom YAML syntax validator (without external libraries) can reliably detect common YAML syntax errors while remaining maintainable and performant.
   430→
   431→**Context**: The hard constraint of no new dependencies forces implementation of a custom validator rather than using established npm packages.
   432→
   433→**Validation Criteria**:
   434→- **CONFIRM if**: Implementation passes test suite covering common errors; startup time < 500ms
   435→- **REJECT if**: Parser misses obvious errors or startup time > 1 second
   436→
   437→**Suggested Method**: CODE_EXPERIMENT (prototype basic parser)
   438→
   439→### HYP-002: Bun.file() Error Codes Match Node.js fs Conventions
   440→
   441→**Status**: PENDING
   442→**Risk Level**: LOW
   443→**Statement**: Bun's file API returns error codes like ENOENT and EACCES for file I/O failures.
   444→
   445→**Context**: Error handling assumes Bun.file() throws errors with `.code` property.
   446→
   447→**Validation Criteria**:
   448→- **CONFIRM if**: Error handling code catches file not found and permission errors correctly
   449→- **REJECT if**: Error codes differ from Node.js convention
   450→
   451→**Suggested Method**: CODEBASE_ANALYSIS (test with actual file operations)
   452→
   453→---
   454→
   455→## Appendix: Command Usage Examples
   456→
   457→### Valid YAML
   458→```bash
   459→$ cat config.yaml
   460→name: my-app
   461→version: 1.0.0
   462→features:
   463→  - logging
   464→  - monitoring
   465→
   466→$ bun run dev validate config.yaml
   467→YAML is valid: config.yaml
   468→$ echo $?
   469→0
   470→```
   471→
   472→### Invalid YAML (unclosed quote)
   473→```bash
   474→$ cat bad.yaml
   475→name: "my-app
   476→version: 1.0.0
   477→
   478→$ bun run dev validate bad.yaml
   479→YAML error in bad.yaml at line 1: Unclosed quote
   480→$ echo $?
   481→1
   482→```
   483→
   484→### File not found
   485→```bash
   486→$ bun run dev validate nonexistent.yaml
   487→File not found: nonexistent.yaml
   488→$ echo $?
   489→1
   490→```

    22→### 2.2 Business Value
    23→
    24→- Enables YAML validation within the project without external dependencies
    25→- Reduces build footprint and deployment complexity
    26→- Provides users a simple, integrated tool for configuration file validation
    27→- Supports configuration-as-code workflows for project users
    28→
    29→### 2.3 Success Metrics
    30→
    31→- YAML validator command successfully validates well-formed YAML files
    32→- YAML validator command successfully rejects malformed YAML files with clear error messages
    33→- No new external dependencies added to the project
    34→- Command integrates seamlessly with existing entry point structure
    35→
    36→## 3. Stakeholders & Users
    37→
    38→### 3.1 User Types
    39→
    40→- **DevOps/Configuration Engineers**: Need to validate YAML configuration files before deployment
    41→- **Project Developers**: Require a quick syntax check during development and testing
    42→- **End Users**: May use the command-line tool as part of their workflow
    43→
    44→### 3.2 Stakeholder Interests
    45→
    46→- **Project Maintainers**: Minimal dependency footprint, clean codebase integration
    47→- **End Users**: Simple, reliable validation with clear error reporting
    48→
    49→## 4. Scope Definition
    50→
    51→### 4.1 In Scope
    52→
    53→- YAML syntax validation (detecting structural errors, syntax violations)
    54→- Command-line interface accepting file path as input
    55→- Clear success and error output messages
    56→- Validation using only existing dependencies (no new package additions)
    57→- Exit codes indicating validation success/failure (0 for success, non-zero for failure)
    58→- Support for standard YAML 1.2 syntax compliance
    59→
    60→### 4.2 Out of Scope
    61→
    62→- Schema validation (enforcing specific YAML structure or field requirements)
    63→- Semantic validation (checking business logic or data consistency rules)
    64→- YAML formatting or auto-correction
    65→- Support for multiple file processing in a single command invocation
    66→- Performance optimization for very large files
    67→- GUI or interactive validation mode
    68→
    69→### 4.3 Assumptions
    70→
    71→- The project has access to a YAML parsing library through existing dependencies or Bun's built-in capabilities
    72→- Users will provide a single file path as input
    73→- Validation output should be human-readable and concise
    74→- Exit code convention (0 = success, non-zero = failure) is acceptable to users
    75→
    76→## 5. Functional Requirements
    77→
    78→### REQ-001: Parse and Validate YAML File
    79→**Priority**: Must Have
    80→**User Type**: DevOps/Configuration Engineers, Project Developers
    81→**Requirement**: The system shall accept a file path argument and parse the specified YAML file to verify it contains valid YAML syntax.
    82→**Rationale**: Core validation functionality is essential for the feature's primary use case.
    83→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    84→- Command accepts file path as argument
    85→- Returns exit code 0 for valid YAML files
    86→- Returns non-zero exit code for invalid YAML files
    87→- Validation completes without throwing unhandled exceptions
    88→
    89→### REQ-002: Display Validation Results
    90→**Priority**: Must Have
    91→**User Type**: DevOps/Configuration Engineers, Project Developers
    92→**Requirement**: The system shall output validation results in a clear, user-friendly format indicating whether the YAML is valid or listing the specific parsing errors encountered.
    93→**Rationale**: Users need clear feedback on validation status and any issues found.
    94→**Acceptance Criteria**:
    95→- Valid YAML: Output confirmation message (e.g., "YAML is valid")
    96→- Invalid YAML: Output specific error message indicating line number and error description
    97→- Error messages are written to stderr
    98→- Success messages are written to stdout
    99→
   100→### REQ-003: Handle Missing or Unreadable Files
   101→**Priority**: Must Have
   102→**User Type**: DevOps/Configuration Engineers, Project Developers
   103→**Requirement**: The system shall gracefully handle cases where the specified file does not exist or cannot be read, providing appropriate error messaging.
   104→**Rationale**: Robust error handling prevents confusing user experience and unclear diagnostics.
   105→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   106→- Returns non-zero exit code when file does not exist
   107→- Returns non-zero exit code when file cannot be read (permission denied, etc.)
   108→- Outputs descriptive error message explaining the issue
   109→- No application crashes or unhandled exceptions
   110→
   111→### REQ-004: No New Dependencies
   112→**Priority**: Must Have
   113→**User Type**: Project Maintainers
   114→**Requirement**: The YAML validator implementation shall use only existing dependencies present in the project and shall not require adding any new external packages.
   115→**Rationale**: Maintains lean dependency footprint and minimizes maintenance burden.
   116→**Acceptance Criteria**:
   117→- `package.json` remains unchanged
   118→- `bun.lockb` or equivalent lock file contains no new entries
   119→- Implementation uses only built-in TypeScript/Bun features or existing packages
   120→- All code is written in TypeScript
   121→
   122→## 6. Non-Functional Requirements
   123→
   124→### 6.1 Performance Expectations
   125→
   126→- Validation should complete within 2 seconds for typical YAML files (< 1 MB)
   127→- Startup time should be minimal (< 500ms)
   128→
   129→### 6.2 Security Requirements
   130→
   131→- Shall not execute arbitrary code or system commands
   132→- Shall not read or process files outside the specified path
   133→- Shall not store validation history or temporary files
   134→
   135→### 6.3 Usability Requirements
   136→
   137→- Command-line syntax should be intuitive and discoverable
   138→- Error messages should be specific enough to help users identify and fix problems
   139→- Output should be suitable for integration into automated scripts (parseable exit codes)
   140→
   141→### 6.4 Compliance Requirements
   142→
   143→- Must comply with YAML 1.2 specification for syntax validation
   144→- Must support UTF-8 encoded files
   145→
   146→## 7. User Stories
   147→
   148→### STORY-001: Quick File Validation During Development
   149→
   150→**As a** Project Developer
   151→**I want to** quickly validate a YAML file from the command line
   152→**So that** I can catch syntax errors before committing or deploying
   153→
   154→**Given** a YAML file with valid syntax
   155→**When** I run the validator on that file
   156→**Then** the command returns exit code 0 and displays a success message
   157→
   158→**Given** a YAML file with syntax errors
   159→**When** I run the validator on that file
   160→**Then** the command returns a non-zero exit code and displays the error location and description
   161→
   162→### STORY-002: Configuration File Pre-Deployment Check
   163→
   164→**As a** DevOps Engineer
   165→**I want to** validate configuration YAML files as part of my deployment pipeline
   166→**So that** invalid configs are caught before they reach production
   167→
   168→**Given** a deployment script that calls the YAML validator
   169→**When** a configuration file is invalid
   170→**Then** the validator exits with a non-zero code, preventing further pipeline steps
   171→
   172→**When** a configuration file is valid
   173→**Then** the validator exits with code 0, allowing the deployment to proceed
   174→
   175→### STORY-003: Error Diagnosis
   176→
   177→**As a** Configuration Engineer
   178→**I want to** understand exactly what's wrong with my YAML file
   179→**So that** I can quickly fix the syntax error
   180→
   181→**Given** a YAML file with a syntax error on line 42
   182→**When** I run the validator
   183→**Then** the error message indicates the line number and type of error encountered
   184→
   185→## 8. Business Rules
   186→
   187→- File validation shall be read-only (no modifications to input files)
   188→- Exit code 0 is reserved for successful validation
   189→- Exit codes 1-255 may be used for various error conditions
   190→- All error output shall include the file path being validated
   191→
   192→## 9. Dependencies & Constraints
   193→
   194→### Dependencies
   195→
   196→- TypeScript (already present)
   197→- Bun runtime (already present)
   198→- Standard library YAML parsing (if available in Bun/Node.js stdlib or existing deps)
   199→
   200→### Constraints
   201→
   202→- Must not add new production dependencies
   203→- Must integrate with existing entry point pattern (index.ts, utils.ts structure)
   204→- Must follow existing code style and conventions in the project
   205→- Maximum scope: single file validation per invocation
   206→
   207→## 10. Clarifications Log
   208→
   209→### AFK Mode: Auto-Selected Defaults
   210→
   211→| Decision Point | Choice | Rationale |
   212→|---|---|---|
   213→| YAML parsing library | Use Bun built-in or existing dependencies | No new deps allowed per requirement; Bun includes YAML support or will defer to valid TypeScript ecosystem existing deps |
   214→| Error message format | Line number + error description + file path | Standard practice for linting/validation tools; helps users diagnose issues quickly |
   215→| Exit code strategy | 0 for success, non-zero for any failure | Unix convention; enables reliable script integration |
   216→| File input method | Single command-line argument (file path) | Simplest, most intuitive CLI pattern |
   217→| Output streams | stdout for success, stderr for errors | Unix convention; enables log capture and filtering |
   218→| Scope: Multiple files | Out of scope (single file only) | Simplifies initial implementation; can be added later |
   219→| YAML version support | 1.2 syntax validation | Most common and widely supported YAML specification |
   220→
   221→### AFK Mode: Inferred Decisions
   222→
   223→| Ambiguity | Resolution | Source |
   224→|---|---|---|
   225→| What type of YAML errors to catch | Syntax/structural errors only (parsing failures) | In-scope definition excludes schema validation; scope focuses on syntactic correctness |
   226→| How to invoke the validator | Command-line argument or dedicated command | Consistent with existing index.ts entry point pattern that accepts process.argv |
   227→| Whether to validate against a schema | No schema validation | Explicitly marked Out of Scope; focus is on syntax validity |
   228→| Handling of special YAML features (anchors, tags, etc.) | Support per YAML 1.2 spec | Standard library or existing YAML library should handle this transparently |

     5→
     6→# Design Document: Simple YAML Validator Command
     7→
     8→**Feature ID**: add a simple yaml validator command without adding new deps
     9→**Version**: 1.0.0
    10→**Created**: 2026-04-11
    11→**Status**: Design Phase
    12→
    13→## 1. Design Overview
    14→
    15→This feature adds a command-line YAML validator to the rp1-eval-project. The validator:
    16→- Accepts a file path as input
    17→- Validates YAML syntax without external dependencies
    18→- Returns appropriate exit codes and user-friendly error messages
    19→- Integrates seamlessly with the existing Bun/TypeScript entry point pattern
    20→
    21→**Key Constraint**: Implementation uses only existing dependencies (TypeScript, Bun, stdlib). A lightweight custom YAML syntax validator replaces external packages.
    22→
    23→### High-Level Architecture
    24→
    25→```
    26→User Command (CLI)
    27→    ↓
    28→src/index.ts (command router)
    29→    ↓
    30→src/yaml-validator.ts (handler)
    31→    ├─ File I/O (Bun.file)
    32→    ├─ validateYamlSyntax() (from utils)
    33→    └─ Output formatting
    34→    ↓
    35→Exit code + stdout/stderr output
    36→```
    37→
    38→---
    39→
    40→## 2. Architecture
    41→
    42→### Component Overview
    43→
    44→| Component | Purpose | Location |
    45→|-----------|---------|----------|
    46→| YAML Syntax Validator | Core validation logic | `src/utils.ts` (new export) |
    47→| File Handler | Reads file, manages I/O errors | `src/yaml-validator.ts` (new) |
    48→| Command Router | Routes CLI commands to handlers | `src/index.ts` (modified) |
    49→| Tests | Validation & integration tests | `src/yaml-validator.test.ts` (new) |
    50→
    51→### Data Flow
    52→
    53→```
    54→1. User runs: bun run dev validate <filepath>
    55→2. index.ts parses argv, detects "validate" command
    56→3. yaml-validator.ts:
    57→   a. Reads file content via Bun.file()
    58→   b. Calls validateYamlSyntax(content)
    59→   c. Formats and outputs result
    60→4. Process exits with appropriate code (0 or 1+)
    61→```
    62→
    63→### Validation Result Contract
    64→
    65→```typescript
    66→interface YamlValidationResult {
    67→  valid: boolean;
    68→  error?: {
    69→    line: number;
    70→    column?: number;
    71→    message: string;
    72→  };
    73→}
    74→```
    75→
    76→---
    77→
    78→## 3. Detailed Design
    79→
    80→### 3.1 YAML Syntax Validator (`src/utils.ts` - New Export)
    81→
    82→**Function**: `validateYamlSyntax(content: string): YamlValidationResult`
    83→
    84→**Validation Rules** (Scope: Basic YAML 1.2 Syntax):
    85→
    86→1. **Indentation**:
    87→   - Consistent indentation (spaces only, no tabs)
    88→   - Valid nesting levels
    89→
    90→2. **Structure Markers**:
    91→   - Paired quotes (single and double)
    92→   - Balanced brackets and braces
    93→   - Valid array markers (-)
    94→   - Valid key-value pairs (:)
    95→
    96→3. **Comments**:
    97→   - Hash (#) comments allowed anywhere
    98→
    99→4. **Strings**:
   100→   - Quoted strings with proper escaping
   101→   - Unquoted strings (basic validation)
   102→   - Multiline strings (basic block detection)
   103→
   104→5. **Collections**:
   105→   - Maps (key: value syntax)
   106→   - Sequences (- item syntax)
   107→   - Nested structures
   108→
   109→**Algorithm**: Line-by-line tokenization with state tracking:
   110→- Track indentation stack
   111→- Detect unclosed quotes
   112→- Validate key-value colons
   113→- Check array marker placement
   114→
   115→**Error Reporting**:
   116→- Return line number and column (if detectable)
   117→- Descriptive message (e.g., "Unclosed quote on line 5")
   118→
   119→**Limitations** (Documented):
   120→- Does not validate against YAML schema
   121→- Does not parse anchors/aliases in detail
   122→- Does not resolve YAML tags
   123→- Focuses on syntactic structure only
   124→
   125→### 3.2 File Handler (`src/yaml-validator.ts` - New File)
   126→
   127→**Function**: `validateYamlFile(filePath: string): Promise<void>`
   128→
   129→**Responsibilities**:
   130→1. Read file using `Bun.file()`
   131→2. Call `validateYamlSyntax()`
   132→3. Format and output results
   133→4. Handle errors (file not found, permission denied, read errors)
   134→5. Exit with appropriate code
   135→
   136→**Error Handling**:
   137→```typescript
   138→try {
   139→  const content = await Bun.file(filePath).text();
   140→  const result = validateYamlSyntax(content);
   141→
   142→  if (result.valid) {
   143→    console.log(`YAML is valid: ${filePath}`);
   144→    process.exit(0);
   145→  } else {
   146→    console.error(
   147→      `YAML error in ${filePath} at line ${result.error.line}: ${result.error.message}`
   148→    );
   149→    process.exit(1);
   150→  }
   151→} catch (error) {
   152→  if (error.code === 'ENOENT') {
   153→    console.error(`File not found: ${filePath}`);
   154→  } else if (error.code === 'EACCES') {
   155→    console.error(`Permission denied: ${filePath}`);
   156→  } else {
   157→    console.error(`Error reading file: ${error.message}`);
   158→  }
   159→  process.exit(1);
   160→}
   161→```
   162→
   163→**Output Streams**:
   164→- **stdout**: Success messages and validation confirmations
   165→- **stderr**: Error messages and diagnostics
   166→
   167→---
   168→
   169→## 4. Technology Stack
   170→
   171→| Layer | Technology | Rationale |
   172→|-------|-----------|-----------|
   173→| Runtime | Bun 1.3.12+ | Already in use; provides fast execution |
   174→| Language | TypeScript (strict mode) | Existing project standard |
   175→| YAML Parsing | Custom syntax validator | No external dependencies allowed; implements basic validation |
   176→| File I/O | `Bun.file()` API | Native Bun support; efficient async file reading |
   177→| Testing | Bun's built-in test runner | Consistent with existing test pattern |
   178→| CLI | `process.argv` | Lightweight; existing pattern in index.ts |
   179→
   180→**No New Dependencies Added**: Implementation uses only existing stack.
   181→
   182→---
   183→
   184→## 5. Implementation Plan
   185→
   186→### T1: Core YAML Syntax Validator
   187→**File**: `src/utils.ts` (add export)
   188→**Tasks**:
   189→1. Define `YamlValidationResult` type
   190→2. Implement `validateYamlSyntax()` function
   191→3. Add indentation validation logic
   192→4. Add quote/bracket balancing checks
   193→5. Add key-value structure validation
   194→6. Handle edge cases (comments, empty lines, multiline strings)
   195→
   196→**Deliverables**:
   197→- Function accepts string, returns result with line number and error description
   198→- Handles typical YAML syntax errors
   199→
   200→### T2: File I/O Handler
   201→**File**: `src/yaml-validator.ts` (new)
   202→**Tasks**:
   203→1. Create `validateYamlFile()` function
   204→2. Implement Bun.file() read with error handling
   205→3. Add file-not-found error detection
   206→4. Add permission-denied error detection
   207→5. Add generic I/O error handling
   208→6. Implement output formatting (success/error messages)
   209→
   210→**Deliverables**:
   211→- Reads file content safely
   212→- Calls validation utility
   213→- Formats and outputs results to correct streams
   214→- Exits with proper codes
   215→
   216→### T3: Command Router
   217→**File**: `src/index.ts` (modify)
   218→**Tasks**:
   219→1. Parse `process.argv` for command intent
   220→2. Detect "validate" command vs. default behavior
   221→3. Route to `validateYamlFile()` if validate command
   222→4. Preserve existing greet functionality for backward compatibility
   223→
   224→**Deliverables**:
   225→- CLI accepts both old format (`bun run dev <name>`) and new (`bun run dev validate <file>`)
   226→- Proper command detection logic
   227→
   228→### T4: Integration Tests
   229→**File**: `src/yaml-validator.test.ts` (new)
   230→**Tasks**:
   231→1. Test valid YAML files
   232→2. Test invalid YAML (bad indentation, unclosed quotes, etc.)
   233→3. Test file not found scenario
   234→4. Test permission denied scenario (if testable)
   235→5. Test exit codes
   236→6. Test output messages
   237→
   238→**Deliverables**:
   239→- Comprehensive test coverage
   240→- Validates all functional requirements
   241→
   242→### T5: Documentation Updates
   243→**File**: Update relevant docs (if applicable)
   244→**Tasks**:
   245→1. Add command usage to README or inline help
   246→2. Document validator limitations
   247→3. Update architecture.md if needed
   248→
   249→**Deliverables**:
   250→- Clear usage documentation
   251→- Known limitations documented
   252→
   253→---
   254→
   255→## 6. Implementation DAG
   256→
   257→**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):
   258→
   259→1. [T1] - Core validator implementation (no dependencies)
   260→2. [T2] - File handler (depends on T1 being complete)
   261→3. [T3] - Command router (depends on T2)
   262→4. [T4] - Tests (depends on T1, T2, T3)
   263→5. [T5] - Documentation (depends on T1, T2, T3)
   264→
   265→**Dependencies**:
   266→
   267→- T2 → T1 (needs validateYamlSyntax API)
   268→- T3 → T2 (routes to file handler)
   269→- T4 → [T1, T2, T3] (tests integrated functionality)
   270→- T5 → [T1, T2, T3] (documents feature)
   271→
   272→**Critical Path**: T1 → T2 → T3 → T4, T5
   273→
   274→---
   275→
   276→## 7. Testing Strategy
   277→
   278→### Test Value Assessment
   279→
   280→| Category | Tests to Design | Rationale |
   281→|----------|-----------------|-----------|
   282→| **Business Logic** | Valid/invalid YAML syntax detection | Core feature; must work correctly |
   283→| **Error Handling** | File I/O errors (not found, permission denied) | Robustness requirement (REQ-003) |
   284→| **Exit Codes** | 0 for success, non-zero for failure | Integration requirement (REQ-001) |
   285→| **Output Messages** | Success and error message format | Usability requirement (REQ-002) |
   286→| **Integration** | End-to-end validation via CLI | System-level requirement |
   287→
   288→### Test Plan
   289→
   290→1. **Unit Tests** (`src/utils.test.ts` additions):
   291→   - `validateYamlSyntax()` with valid YAML
   292→   - `validateYamlSyntax()` with invalid indentation
   293→   - `validateYamlSyntax()` with unclosed quotes
   294→   - `validateYamlSyntax()` with malformed key-value
   295→   - `validateYamlSyntax()` with unbalanced braces/brackets
   296→
   297→2. **Integration Tests** (`src/yaml-validator.test.ts`):
   298→   - Valid file validation (exit code 0)
   299→   - Invalid file validation (exit code 1)
   300→   - File not found (exit code 1, error message)
   301→   - Output stream routing (stdout vs stderr)
   302→
   303→3. **Manual Testing** (pre-release):
   304→   - Real YAML configuration files
   305→   - Edge cases (large files, special characters)
   306→   - Performance validation (< 2 seconds for 1MB files)
   307→
   308→---
   309→
   310→## 8. Deployment Design
   311→
   312→### Entry Point Changes
   313→
   314→**Current** (`src/index.ts`):
   315→```typescript
   316→import { greet } from "./utils";
   317→const name = process.argv[2] ?? "World";
   318→console.log(greet(name));
   319→```
   320→
   321→**New** (`src/index.ts`):
   322→```typescript
   323→import { greet } from "./utils";
   324→import { validateYamlFile } from "./yaml-validator";
   325→
   326→const command = process.argv[2];
   327→const arg = process.argv[3];
   328→
   329→if (command === "validate") {
   330→  if (!arg) {
   331→    console.error("Usage: validate <filepath>");
   332→    process.exit(1);
   333→  }
   334→  await validateYamlFile(arg);
   335→} else {
   336→  const name = command ?? "World";
   337→  console.log(greet(name));
   338→}
   339→```
   340→
   341→### Backward Compatibility
   342→
   343→- Existing `bun run dev <name>` continues to work
   344→- New `bun run dev validate <file>` adds new functionality
   345→- No breaking changes to existing CLI behavior
   346→
   347→### Execution Path
   348→
   349→```bash
   350→# Existing usage (unchanged)
   351→$ bun run dev Alice
   352→Hello, Alice!
   353→
   354→# New usage
   355→$ bun run dev validate config.yaml
   356→YAML is valid: config.yaml
   357→
   358→$ bun run dev validate bad.yaml
   359→YAML error in bad.yaml at line 5: Unclosed quote
   360→```
   361→
   362→---
   363→
   364→## 9. Documentation Impact
   365→
   366→| Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale |
   367→|------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------|
   368→| add | README.md | Usage section | (new content) | Document new validate command |
   369→| add | src/yaml-validator.ts | JSDoc comments | patterns.md | Follow existing doc conventions |
   370→| add | src/utils.ts | JSDoc for validateYamlSyntax | patterns.md | Document new utility function |
   371→| edit | architecture.md (if exists) | Components section | architecture.md | Note new file handler component |
   372→
   373→---
   374→
   375→## 10. Design Decisions Log
   376→
   377→| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives |
   378→|----|----------|--------|-----------|--------------|
   379→| D1 | YAML parsing approach | Custom lightweight validator (no external deps) | REQ-004 forbids new dependencies; custom parser avoids adding `js-yaml` or `yaml` | Use existing npm package, shell out to external tool |
   380→| D2 | Validation scope | Basic syntax validation only | Matches in-scope requirements; schema validation out of scope | Full semantic validation, schema enforcement |
   381→| D3 | File I/O | Use `Bun.file()` API | Native Bun support, efficient async I/O | Node.js fs module, Deno API |
   382→| D4 | Command routing | Parse argv for "validate" subcommand | Simple, matches existing entry point pattern | Dedicated CLI framework (Commander, yargs) |
   383→| D5 | Output streams | stdout for success, stderr for errors | Unix convention; enables log filtering | All output to stdout, single output stream |
   384→| D6 | Exit codes | 0 for success, 1 for all failures | Standard Unix convention; simple for scripting | Different codes for different errors |
   385→| D7 | Error line number | Included in error output | User diagnostic requirement (REQ-002) | Generic error message only |
   386→| D8 | Single vs. batch | Single file per invocation | Scope constraint; simpler implementation | Validate multiple files in one run |
   387→
   388→---
   389→
   390→## 11. Technical Design Notes
   391→
   392→### YAML Validation Approach
   393→
   394→The custom YAML validator uses a **line-by-line tokenization strategy**:
   395→
   396→1. **Tokenize**: Split content into lines, parse each line for structure
   397→2. **Track State**: Maintain stack of indentation levels, quote states
   398→3. **Validate Rules**:
   399→   - Indentation consistency (spaces only)
   400→   - Quote pairing (single/double)
   401→   - Bracket matching
   402→   - Key-value colon placement
   403→   - Array marker validity
   404→
   405→4. **Early Exit**: Return first error encountered with line number
   406→
   407→**Why not a full YAML parser?**
   408→- Would require parsing complex YAML features (anchors, aliases, tags, multiline strings)
   409→- Would likely need an external library, violating REQ-004
   410→- Syntax validation is sufficient for catching common errors
   411→
   412→### Known Limitations
   413→
   414→- **Anchors & Aliases**: `&anchor` and `*alias` not fully validated
   415→- **Tags**: Custom YAML tags (e.g., `!!str`) validated minimally
   416→- **Multiline Strings**: Basic detection only; complex folding/block rules not fully enforced
   417→- **Escape Sequences**: Basic escaping checked; complex Unicode escapes not fully validated
   418→
   419→**Mitigation**: Document these limitations clearly. Users with complex YAML should use dedicated tools.
   420→
   421→---
   422→
   423→## 12. Hypothesis Validation (AFK Auto-Decisions)
   424→
   425→### HYP-001: Custom YAML Parser Can Validate Basic Syntax
   426→
   427→**Status**: PENDING
   428→**Risk Level**: MEDIUM
   429→**Statement**: A custom YAML syntax validator (without external libraries) can reliably detect common YAML syntax errors while remaining maintainable and performant.
   430→
   431→**Context**: The hard constraint of no new dependencies forces implementation of a custom validator rather than using established npm packages.
   432→
   433→**Validation Criteria**:
   434→- **CONFIRM if**: Implementation passes test suite covering common errors; startup time < 500ms
   435→- **REJECT if**: Parser misses obvious errors or startup time > 1 second
   436→
   437→**Suggested Method**: CODE_EXPERIMENT (prototype basic parser)
   438→
   439→### HYP-002: Bun.file() Error Codes Match Node.js fs Conventions
   440→
   441→**Status**: PENDING
   442→**Risk Level**: LOW
   443→**Statement**: Bun's file API returns error codes like ENOENT and EACCES for file I/O failures.
   444→
   445→**Context**: Error handling assumes Bun.file() throws errors with `.code` property.
   446→
   447→**Validation Criteria**:
   448→- **CONFIRM if**: Error handling code catches file not found and permission errors correctly
   449→- **REJECT if**: Error codes differ from Node.js convention
   450→
   451→**Suggested Method**: CODEBASE_ANALYSIS (test with actual file operations)
   452→
   453→---
   454→
   455→## Appendix: Command Usage Examples
   456→
   457→### Valid YAML
   458→```bash
   459→$ cat config.yaml
   460→name: my-app
   461→version: 1.0.0
   462→features:
   463→  - logging
   464→  - monitoring
   465→
   466→$ bun run dev validate config.yaml
   467→YAML is valid: config.yaml
   468→$ echo $?
   469→0
   470→```
   471→
   472→### Invalid YAML (unclosed quote)
   473→```bash
   474→$ cat bad.yaml
   475→name: "my-app
   476→version: 1.0.0
   477→
   478→$ bun run dev validate bad.yaml
   479→YAML error in bad.yaml at line 1: Unclosed quote
   480→$ echo $?
   481→1
   482→```
   483→
   484→### File not found
   485→```bash
   486→$ bun run dev validate nonexistent.yaml
   487→File not found: nonexistent.yaml
   488→$ echo $?
   489→1
   490→```
   491→

    15→This feature adds a command-line YAML validator to the rp1-eval-project. The validator:
    16→- Accepts a file path as input

    53→```

    57→   a. Reads file content via Bun.file()
    58→   b. Calls validateYamlSyntax(content)
    59→   c. Formats and outputs result

    61→```
    62→

    64→

    66→interface YamlValidationResult {

    96→3. **Comments**:
    97→   - Hash (#) comments allowed anywhere
    98→
    99→4. **Strings**:
   100→   - Quoted strings with proper escaping
   101→   - Unquoted strings (basic validation)
   102→   - Multiline strings (basic block detection)
   103→
   104→5. **Collections**:
   105→   - Maps (key: value syntax)
   106→   - Sequences (- item syntax)
   107→   - Nested structures

   125→### 3.2 File Handler (`src/yaml-validator.ts` - New File)

   138→try {

   140→  const result = validateYamlSyntax(content);
   141→
   142→  if (result.valid) {

   310→## 8. Deployment Design
   311→
   312→### Entry Point Changes
   313→
   314→**Current** (`src/index.ts`):

   320→
   321→**New** (`src/index.ts`):
   322→```typescript
   323→import { greet } from "./utils";
   324→import { validateYamlFile } from "./yaml-validator";
   325→
   326→const command = process.argv[2];
   327→const arg = process.argv[3];
   328→
   329→if (command === "validate") {
   330→  if (!arg) {
   331→    console.error("Usage: validate <filepath>");
   332→    process.exit(1);
   333→  }
   334→  await validateYamlFile(arg);
   335→} else {
   336→  const name = command ?? "World";

   344→- New `bun run dev validate <file>` adds new functionality

   346→
   347→### Execution Path
   348→
   349→```bash
   350→# Existing usage (unchanged)
   351→$ bun run dev Alice
   352→Hello, Alice!
   353→
   354→# New usage
   355→$ bun run dev validate config.yaml
   356→YAML is valid: config.yaml
   357→
   358→$ bun run dev validate bad.yaml

   360→```

   363→
   364→## 9. Documentation Impact
   365→

   369→| add | src/yaml-validator.ts | JSDoc comments | patterns.md | Follow existing doc conventions |
   370→| add | src/utils.ts | JSDoc for validateYamlSyntax | patterns.md | Document new utility function |
   371→| edit | architecture.md (if exists) | Components section | architecture.md | Note new file handler component |
   372→
   373→---
   374→
   375→## 10. Design Decisions Log
   376→
   377→| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives |
   378→|----|----------|--------|-----------|--------------|
   379→| D1 | YAML parsing approach | Custom lightweight validator (no external deps) | REQ-004 forbids new dependencies; custom parser avoids adding `js-yaml` or `yaml` | Use existing npm package, shell out to external tool |
   380→| D2 | Validation scope | Basic syntax validation only | Matches in-scope requirements; schema validation out of scope | Full semantic validation, schema enforcement |
   381→| D3 | File I/O | Use `Bun.file()` API | Native Bun support, efficient async I/O | Node.js fs module, Deno API |
   382→| D4 | Command routing | Parse argv for "validate" subcommand | Simple, matches existing entry point pattern | Dedicated CLI framework (Commander, yargs) |
   383→| D5 | Output streams | stdout for success, stderr for errors | Unix convention; enables log filtering | All output to stdout, single output stream |
   384→| D6 | Exit codes | 0 for success, 1 for all failures | Standard Unix convention; simple for scripting | Different codes for different errors |
   385→| D7 | Error line number | Included in error output | User diagnostic requirement (REQ-002) | Generic error message only |
   386→| D8 | Single vs. batch | Single file per invocation | Scope constraint; simpler implementation | Validate multiple files in one run |
   387→
   388→---
   389→
   390→## 11. Technical Design Notes
   391→
   392→### YAML Validation Approach
   393→
   394→The custom YAML validator uses a **line-by-line tokenization strategy**:
   395→
   396→1. **Tokenize**: Split content into lines, parse each line for structure
   397→2. **Track State**: Maintain stack of indentation levels, quote states
   398→3. **Validate Rules**:
   399→   - Indentation consistency (spaces only)
   400→   - Quote pairing (single/double)
   401→   - Bracket matching
   402→   - Key-value colon placement
   403→   - Array marker validity
   404→
   405→4. **Early Exit**: Return first error encountered with line number
   406→
   407→**Why not a full YAML parser?**
   408→- Would require parsing complex YAML features (anchors, aliases, tags, multiline strings)
   409→- Would likely need an external library, violating REQ-004
   410→- Syntax validation is sufficient for catching common errors
   411→
   412→### Known Limitations
   413→
   414→- **Anchors & Aliases**: `&anchor` and `*alias` not fully validated
   415→- **Tags**: Custom YAML tags (e.g., `!!str`) validated minimally
   416→- **Multiline Strings**: Basic detection only; complex folding/block rules not fully enforced
   417→- **Escape Sequences**: Basic escaping checked; complex Unicode escapes not fully validated
   418→
   419→**Mitigation**: Document these limitations clearly. Users with complex YAML should use dedicated tools.
   420→
   421→---
   422→
   423→## 12. Hypothesis Validation (AFK Auto-Decisions)
   424→
   425→### HYP-001: Custom YAML Parser Can Validate Basic Syntax
   426→
   427→**Status**: PENDING
   428→**Risk Level**: MEDIUM
   429→**Statement**: A custom YAML syntax validator (without external libraries) can reliably detect common YAML syntax errors while remaining maintainable and performant.
   430→
   431→**Context**: The hard constraint of no new dependencies forces implementation of a custom validator rather than using established npm packages.
   432→
   433→**Validation Criteria**:
   434→- **CONFIRM if**: Implementation passes test suite covering common errors; startup time < 500ms
   435→- **REJECT if**: Parser misses obvious errors or startup time > 1 second
   436→
   437→**Suggested Method**: CODE_EXPERIMENT (prototype basic parser)
   438→
   439→### HYP-002: Bun.file() Error Codes Match Node.js fs Conventions
   440→
   441→**Status**: PENDING
   442→**Risk Level**: LOW
   443→**Statement**: Bun's file API returns error codes like ENOENT and EACCES for file I/O failures.
   444→
   445→**Context**: Error handling assumes Bun.file() throws errors with `.code` property.
   446→
   447→**Validation Criteria**:
   448→- **CONFIRM if**: Error handling code catches file not found and permission errors correctly
   449→- **REJECT if**: Error codes differ from Node.js convention
   450→
   451→**Suggested Method**: CODEBASE_ANALYSIS (test with actual file operations)
   452→
   453→---
   454→
   455→## Appendix: Command Usage Examples
   456→
   457→### Valid YAML
   458→```bash
   459→$ cat config.yaml
   460→name: my-app
   461→version: 1.0.0
   462→features:
   463→  - logging
   464→  - monitoring
   465→
   466→$ bun run dev validate config.yaml
   467→YAML is valid: config.yaml
   468→$ echo $?
   469→0
   470→```
   471→
   472→### Invalid YAML (unclosed quote)
   473→```bash
   474→$ cat bad.yaml
   475→name: "my-app
   476→version: 1.0.0
   477→
   478→$ bun run dev validate bad.yaml
   479→YAML error in bad.yaml at line 1: Unclosed quote
   480→$ echo $?
   481→1
   482→```
   483→
   484→### File not found
   485→```bash
   486→$ bun run dev validate nonexistent.yaml
   487→File not found: nonexistent.yaml
   488→$ echo $?
   489→1
   490→```

# Requirements Specification: Simple YAML Validator Command

**Feature ID**: add a simple yaml validator command without adding new deps
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-04-11

## 1. Feature Overview

Add a command-line interface that validates YAML files for syntactic correctness without introducing any new external dependencies. This feature extends the existing utility scripting project to support YAML validation as a built-in capability using only the standard library and existing dependencies.

## 2. Business Context

### 2.1 Problem Statement

Users need a lightweight way to validate YAML configuration files from the command line. Currently, the project lacks this capability and adding it via external packages would increase dependency overhead and maintenance burden.

### 2.2 Business Value

- Enables YAML validation within the project without external dependencies
- Reduces build footprint and deployment complexity
- Provides users a simple, integrated tool for configuration file validation
- Supports configuration-as-code workflows for project users

### 2.3 Success Metrics

- YAML validator command successfully validates well-formed YAML files
- YAML validator command successfully rejects malformed YAML files with clear error messages
- No new external dependencies added to the project
- Command integrates seamlessly with existing entry point structure

## 3. Stakeholders & Users

### 3.1 User Types

- **DevOps/Configuration Engineers**: Need to validate YAML configuration files before deployment
- **Project Developers**: Require a quick syntax check during development and testing
- **End Users**: May use the command-line tool as part of their workflow

### 3.2 Stakeholder Interests

- **Project Maintainers**: Minimal dependency footprint, clean codebase integration
- **End Users**: Simple, reliable validation with clear error reporting

## 4. Scope Definition

### 4.1 In Scope

- YAML syntax validation (detecting structural errors, syntax violations)
- Command-line interface accepting file path as input
- Clear success and error output messages
- Validation using only existing dependencies (no new package additions)
- Exit codes indicating validation success/failure (0 for success, non-zero for failure)
- Support for standard YAML 1.2 syntax compliance

### 4.2 Out of Scope

- Schema validation (enforcing specific YAML structure or field requirements)
- Semantic validation (checking business logic or data consistency rules)
- YAML formatting or auto-correction
- Support for multiple file processing in a single command invocation
- Performance optimization for very large files
- GUI or interactive validation mode

### 4.3 Assumptions

- The project has access to a YAML parsing library through existing dependencies or Bun's built-in capabilities
- Users will provide a single file path as input
- Validation output should be human-readable and concise
- Exit code convention (0 = success, non-zero = failure) is acceptable to users

## 5. Functional Requirements

### REQ-001: Parse and Validate YAML File
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: DevOps/Configuration Engineers, Project Developers
**Requirement**: The system shall accept a file path argument and parse the specified YAML file to verify it contains valid YAML syntax.
**Rationale**: Core validation functionality is essential for the feature's primary use case.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Command accepts file path as argument
- Returns exit code 0 for valid YAML files
- Returns non-zero exit code for invalid YAML files
- Validation completes without throwing unhandled exceptions

### REQ-002: Display Validation Results
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: DevOps/Configuration Engineers, Project Developers
**Requirement**: The system shall output validation results in a clear, user-friendly format indicating whether the YAML is valid or listing the specific parsing errors encountered.
**Rationale**: Users need clear feedback on validation status and any issues found.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Valid YAML: Output confirmation message (e.g., "YAML is valid")
- Invalid YAML: Output specific error message indicating line number and error description
- Error messages are written to stderr
- Success messages are written to stdout

### REQ-003: Handle Missing or Unreadable Files
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: DevOps/Configuration Engineers, Project Developers
**Requirement**: The system shall gracefully handle cases where the specified file does not exist or cannot be read, providing appropriate error messaging.
**Rationale**: Robust error handling prevents confusing user experience and unclear diagnostics.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Returns non-zero exit code when file does not exist
- Returns non-zero exit code when file cannot be read (permission denied, etc.)
- Outputs descriptive error message explaining the issue
- No application crashes or unhandled exceptions

### REQ-004: No New Dependencies
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Project Maintainers
**Requirement**: The YAML validator implementation shall use only existing dependencies present in the project and shall not require adding any new external packages.
**Rationale**: Maintains lean dependency footprint and minimizes maintenance burden.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- `package.json` remains unchanged
- `bun.lockb` or equivalent lock file contains no new entries
- Implementation uses only built-in TypeScript/Bun features or existing packages
- All code is written in TypeScript

## 6. Non-Functional Requirements

### 6.1 Performance Expectations

- Validation should complete within 2 seconds for typical YAML files (< 1 MB)
- Startup time should be minimal (< 500ms)

### 6.2 Security Requirements

- Shall not execute arbitrary code or system commands
- Shall not read or process files outside the specified path
- Shall not store validation history or temporary files

### 6.3 Usability Requirements

- Command-line syntax should be intuitive and discoverable
- Error messages should be specific enough to help users identify and fix problems
- Output should be suitable for integration into automated scripts (parseable exit codes)

### 6.4 Compliance Requirements

- Must comply with YAML 1.2 specification for syntax validation
- Must support UTF-8 encoded files

## 7. User Stories

### STORY-001: Quick File Validation During Development

**As a** Project Developer
**I want to** quickly validate a YAML file from the command line
**So that** I can catch syntax errors before committing or deploying

**Given** a YAML file with valid syntax
**When** I run the validator on that file
**Then** the command returns exit code 0 and displays a success message

**Given** a YAML file with syntax errors
**When** I run the validator on that file
**Then** the command returns a non-zero exit code and displays the error location and description

### STORY-002: Configuration File Pre-Deployment Check

**As a** DevOps Engineer
**I want to** validate configuration YAML files as part of my deployment pipeline
**So that** invalid configs are caught before they reach production

**Given** a deployment script that calls the YAML validator
**When** a configuration file is invalid
**Then** the validator exits with a non-zero code, preventing further pipeline steps

**When** a configuration file is valid
**Then** the validator exits with code 0, allowing the deployment to proceed

### STORY-003: Error Diagnosis

**As a** Configuration Engineer
**I want to** understand exactly what's wrong with my YAML file
**So that** I can quickly fix the syntax error

**Given** a YAML file with a syntax error on line 42
**When** I run the validator
**Then** the error message indicates the line number and type of error encountered

## 8. Business Rules

- File validation shall be read-only (no modifications to input files)
- Exit code 0 is reserved for successful validation
- Exit codes 1-255 may be used for various error conditions
- All error output shall include the file path being validated

## 9. Dependencies & Constraints

### Dependencies

- TypeScript (already present)
- Bun runtime (already present)
- Standard library YAML parsing (if available in Bun/Node.js stdlib or existing deps)

### Constraints

- Must not add new production dependencies
- Must integrate with existing entry point pattern (index.ts, utils.ts structure)
- Must follow existing code style and conventions in the project
- Maximum scope: single file validation per invocation

## 10. Clarifications Log

### AFK Mode: Auto-Selected Defaults

| Decision Point | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| YAML parsing library | Use Bun built-in or existing dependencies | No new deps allowed per requirement; Bun includes YAML support or will defer to valid TypeScript ecosystem existing deps |
| Error message format | Line number + error description + file path | Standard practice for linting/validation tools; helps users diagnose issues quickly |
| Exit code strategy | 0 for success, non-zero for any failure | Unix convention; enables reliable script integration |
| File input method | Single command-line argument (file path) | Simplest, most intuitive CLI pattern |
| Output streams | stdout for success, stderr for errors | Unix convention; enables log capture and filtering |
| Scope: Multiple files | Out of scope (single file only) | Simplifies initial implementation; can be added later |
| YAML version support | 1.2 syntax validation | Most common and widely supported YAML specification |

### AFK Mode: Inferred Decisions

| Ambiguity | Resolution | Source |
|---|---|---|
| What type of YAML errors to catch | Syntax/structural errors only (parsing failures) | In-scope definition excludes schema validation; scope focuses on syntactic correctness |
